items.informal_name: Injectivity of Multivariate Polynomial Expansion Homomorphism for Positive Exponents
items.type: ∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → Function.Injective ⇑(MvPolynomial.expand n)
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $ and type $ \sigma $, the algebra homomorphism that maps each variable $ X_i $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ to $ X_i^n $ is injective when $ n $ is a positive integer. This homomorphism preserves the algebra structure over $ R $ and raises each variable to the $ n $-th power.

items.informal_name: Compatibility of Partial Derivatives with Renaming in Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} [inst : CommSemiring R] {τ : Type u_1} {f : σ → τ},
  Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (x : σ) (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
      (MvPolynomial.pderiv (f x)) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) p) = (MvPolynomial.rename f) ((MvPolynomial.pderiv x) p)
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative semiring, $ \sigma, \tau $ be variable index sets, and $ f : \sigma \to \tau $ an injective map. For any polynomial $ p \in R[\sigma] $ and variable $ x \in \sigma $, the partial derivative operator commutes with renaming variables via $ f $: $ \frac{\partial}{\partial (f(x))} (p^f) = (\frac{\partial p}{\partial x})^f $, where $ p^f $ denotes the polynomial obtained by renaming variables according to $ f $.

items.informal_name: Jacobi Matrix Entries for Naive Pre-Submersive Presentation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {ι : Type w} {σ : Type t} [inst : CommRing R] {v : ι → MvPolynomial σ R} (a : ι → σ)
  (ha : Function.Injective a)
  (s : optParam (MvPolynomial σ R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range v) → MvPolynomial σ R) (Function.surjInv ⋯))
  (hs :
    autoParam
      (∀ (x : MvPolynomial σ R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range v)), (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span (Set.range v))) (s x) = x)
      _auto_103✝)
  [inst_1 : Fintype ι] [inst_2 : DecidableEq ι] (i j : ι),
  (Algebra.PreSubmersivePresentation.naive a ha...
items.informal_description: For a finite type $\iota$ with decidable equality, the $(i,j)$-entry of the Jacobi matrix of the naive pre-submersive presentation is equal to the partial derivative of the relation $v_j$ with respect to the generator $a_i$ in the polynomial ring $R[\sigma]$. This establishes that the matrix is formed by evaluating $\partial_{a_i}(v_j)$ for all indices $i,j : \iota$.
